perturbed_solution: $2f(4)=g(4)$, so $2\left(16-8-m\right)=16-4+4m$. Expanding the left-hand side gives $16+2m=8-4m$, or $6m=-8$ and $m=\boxed{-\frac{4}{3}}$.

errors.rationale: The substitution for f(4) should be 16-8+m; flipping the sign of m to -m changes f(4) incorrectly.
For g(4), x^2-2x+4m at x=4 is 16-8+4m; computing 16-8 as 16-4 is incorrect because 16-8=8.
The expression 16-8+4m simplifies to 8+4m, so the expansion should keep +4m on the right side; changing it to -4m mishandles the sign.
